discovery: Development of massively parallel next-generation DNA sequencing (sequencing by synthesis with reversible terminators on clonal clusters)
rationale: After physical-chemistry and materials prizes in 2023 (quantum dots) and 2025 (MOFs), and a computational-biology prize in 2024, the committee often turns to chemistry that has transformed the life sciences. The chemistry behind Solexa/Illumina sequencing-by-synthesis brought the cost of genome sequencing down by about a million-fold, and it now underpins genomics, diagnostics and precision medicine. Its inventors have already won major prizes, including the Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences, which are typical signs that a Nobel is likely.
